newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'BISHI MOTORS TO MAKE FEWER CARS FOR THAI MARKET.
newsitem.headline: M'BISHI MOTORS TO MAKE FEWER CARS FOR THAI MARKET.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Corp said on Thursday that it planned to produce fewer vehicles in Thailand for the Thai domestic market in calendar 1997 due to inventory adjustments.
But it will produce more vehicles in Thailand for export in 1997 as part of a company-wide restructuring of output, a company spokesman said.
Mitsubishi plans to produce a total of 50,000 cars and pick-up trucks at its Thai plants in 1997 for the Thai market against an actual output of 73,000 in 1996, the spokesman said.
The car maker plans to produce 38,000 pick-up trucks in Thailand in 1997 for export against its actual output of 12,000 in 1996, he said.
Demand for cars in Thailand has been slow since the end of last year, Japanese car industry officials said.

The Mitsubishi spokesman said that production of vehicles for export would grow in 1997 as the company had completed transferring production of pick-up trucks from its plant in Nagoya, Japan, to Thailand.
The spokesman said that the company is still considering what measures to take to cope with economic restructuring plans announced by Thailand recently.

"It will take some time before the effect from the flotation of the baht becomes clear. We think, however, that it will probably further dampen demand but it will be good for exports," the spokesman said.
